title: Will France's 2027 soft wheat harvest come in below 30 million tonnes?

masked.note: Commodity names and calendar dates are hidden; months are relative to now (t0) and prices are an index, 100 at t-12.

forecasts.name: Climate Pessimist · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: French soft wheat is intensely vulnerable to erratic winter rain followed by spring heat domes. A sub-30Mt harvest is heavily under-priced.

forecasts.name: Land-Grab Realist · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Persistent warming anomalies and erratic precipitation patterns make sub-30 million tonne harvests the new, high-probability baseline for French soft wheat.

forecasts.name: BirdLife Europe, EEB, WWF and Greenpeace (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Extreme weather volatility, wet planting seasons, and degraded soil health make French harvests falling below 30Mt an acute ongoing risk.

forecasts.name: Copa-Cogeca (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Escalating weather extremes and excessive regulatory burdens on French growers heighten the risk of subpar wheat harvests below 30Mt.

forecasts.name: Crowd Follower · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Market is 46%. European weather anomalies are balanced against normal base production rates, so I stay with the crowd.

forecasts.name: Macro / Dollar · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Specific national harvest volumes reflect idiosyncratic factors secondary to the broad grain complex; slight bias to baseline mean.

forecasts.name: Geopolitics Hawk · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Sub-30Mt crops are rare historically, but persistent climatic instability and input cost pressures maintain substantial risk.

forecasts.name: IMF (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Elevated European climate variability weighs on yield predictability, though widespread acreage collapse below 30 Mt remains a downside risk.

forecasts.name: IFPRI (Joseph Glauber) (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Sub-30 mt harvests require catastrophic weather; while European heat anomalies are elevated, baseline acreage and input adoption keep the median crop higher.

forecasts.name: FAO (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: While climate variability is increasing, standard acreage and normal weather recovery typically keep French soft wheat above 30 million tonnes.

forecasts.name: Scott Irwin (farmdoc) (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Sub-30 Mt harvests are rare historical anomalies for France; acreage and input management generally rebound following poor crop years.

forecasts.name: USDA WASDE (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Our bottom-up modeling assumes trend yields for 2027; a sub-30 million tonne harvest represents an abnormal deviation requiring major weather failures.

forecasts.name: European Commission DG AGRI (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: EU arable crops show broad resilience; projected yield recoveries make a sub-30M tonne French soft wheat harvest an outlier scenario.

forecasts.name: Agronomist · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Sub-30 million tonne harvests require acute weather failure across both flowering and filling windows. A normal seasonal distribution favors yields closer to the 34 Mt norm.

forecasts.name: Efficient-Market Skeptic · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Crop failures below 30 million tonnes are historic outliers for French wheat. Weather anomalies mean-revert, making extreme output deficits improbable.

forecasts.name: Adaptation Optimist · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: French agronomy, improved seed genetics, and shifting planting tactics routinely beat sub-30Mt doom forecasts.
